label: ingest package — SPEC §3 compliance review

findings.description: RST heading detection broken: RST patterns use multi-line regex (/^(.+)\n[=]+\s*$/m) but the code iterates single lines (line 74: for each line). A single line never contains \n, so the regex never matches. RST documents always fall through to the 'no headings found' branch (line 93) and return as a single chunk. The spec (§3A, Feature changes) lists RST as a supported heading format.
findings.fix_sketch: Reformulate RST detection as two-pass: find underline-like lines (=====, -----, etc.) by line inspection, then pair each underline with the preceding non-blank line as the heading. Alternatively, match against raw document (not line-split) using the existing regex, then map match positions back to line numbers.

findings.description: Document preamble silently dropped: text before the first heading is never emitted as a chunk. The loop starts from the first heading (headings[0]), and buildHeadingPath only produces chunks for heading-delimited sections. Lines 0 through (firstHeading.line - 1) are discarded. This affects documents with title blocks, YAML front matter, or introductory paragraphs before any heading.
findings.fix_sketch: Before the heading loop, check if the first heading is at line > 0. If so, emit lines[0..firstHeading.line-1] as a preamble chunk with metadata.isHeadingRoot = true.

findings.description: Code preamble silently dropped: non-declaration lines before the first declaration (e.g. imports, module-level config) are skipped and not emitted as chunks. The 'emit preceding non-declaration lines' logic (line 94) only runs when chunks.length > 0, so it never fires for the first declaration. This discards imports, directives, and top-level constants.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a preamble check before the first declaration: if the first declaration starts at line > 0, emit lines[0..firstDecl.startLine-1] as a preamble chunk before processing declarations.

findings.description: Vacuous test: 'throws for unsupported language' uses AstChunker('typescript') (which IS a supported language) and calls expect(() => chunker.chunk('code', {})) without .toThrow() matcher. The assertion is a no-op — the test always passes regardless of whether the chunker throws. The unsupported-language code path is never exercised.
findings.fix_sketch: Change to: const chunker = new AstChunker('unsupported'); expect(() => chunker.chunk('code')).toThrow(PermanentChunkingError);

findings.description: Vacuous test: 'throws for unsupported syntax' uses HeadingChunker('markdown') (supported) and calls expect(() => chunker.chunk('text')) without .toThrow() matcher. The assertion is a no-op. The unsupported-syntax error path is never exercised.
findings.fix_sketch: Change to: const chunker = new HeadingChunker('unknown'); expect(() => chunker.chunk('text')).toThrow(PermanentChunkingError);

findings.description: ChunkerRegistry not sealed: SPEC §3A requires 'Chunker registry is append-only at build time — no runtime registration from untrusted sources' and Decision D4 says 'registry is sealed after module initialization'. The instance-based ChunkerRegistry in chunker-registry.ts has no seal() mechanism — register() can be called at any time. A separate static/sealed ChunkerRegistry exists in registry.ts but is unused.
findings.fix_sketch: Either: (a) add a seal() method and static sealed flag to the instance-based ChunkerRegistry, calling it after auto-registration in index.ts, or (b) replace the instance-based registry with the static sealed one from registry.ts.

findings.description: Python chunking uses brace-depth tracking but Python uses indentation, not braces. extractDeclaration() counts {/(/}/) for boundary detection. For Python code, depth never increases from braces (Python has no braces), and counting parentheses causes false boundaries (e.g. a multi-line function call would terminate the declaration early). The spec lists Python as a supported language.
findings.fix_sketch: For Python, replace brace-depth tracking with indentation-based boundary detection: track the indentation level of the declaration line, then find the first subsequent line with equal or lesser indentation.

findings.description: Short declarations (< minFunctionLines) silently dropped: when extractDeclaration returns a declaration whose body is shorter than minFunctionLines, the code does NOT emit it as a chunk AND does NOT re-attach its lines to another chunk. The lines of a short function/class are simply skipped. The spec says 'Functions shorter than this are merged into the preceding chunk' (ChunkerOptions.minFunctionLines description), not dropped.
findings.fix_sketch: When declLines < minLines, do not skip — instead, merge the declaration's lines into the preceding chunk (or buffer them to merge into the next declaration).

findings.description: Dead code: errors.ts defines PermanentChunkingError and TransientChunkingError identical to those in chunker-registry.ts. No file imports from errors.ts. It is compiled into dist/ (errors.js, errors.d.ts), polluting the build artifact.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete errors.ts. The canonical error classes are in chunker-registry.ts and are re-exported from index.ts.

findings.description: Dead code: registry.ts defines a completely separate static/sealed ChunkerRegistry that is never imported or referenced by any other file. It is compiled into dist/ (registry.js, registry.d.ts).
findings.fix_sketch: Either delete registry.ts (if chunker-registry.ts is the canonical version) or wire it into index.ts with a seal() call after auto-registration.

findings.description: HeadingChunker tests only cover Markdown. No tests for MDX, RST, or AsciiDoc. The RST bug (see critical finding) would have been caught with an RST test.
findings.fix_sketch: Add unit tests for each format: MDX (similar to markdown), RST (with underline-style headings), AsciiDoc (with =-style headings).

findings.description: AstChunker tests only cover TypeScript. No tests for Python, Java, or C#. The Python boundary-detection issue (see above) would have been caught with a Python test.
findings.fix_sketch: Add unit tests for Python (def/class, indentation), Java (class/method declarations), and C# (class/interface/struct declarations).

findings.description: No test asserts that sourceMap is present and non-null on every chunk. SPEC requires 'every chunk carries a source map — zero chunks without provenance.'
findings.fix_sketch: In each chunking test, add: chunks.forEach(c => { expect(c.sourceMap).toBeDefined(); expect(typeof c.sourceMap.sourceStartLine).toBe('number'); expect(typeof c.sourceMap.sourceEndLine).toBe('number'); });

findings.description: estimate() only tested for HeadingChunker. AstChunker.estimate() is untested. The estimate returns coarse counts that may be inaccurate for nested or multi-line declarations.
findings.fix_sketch: Add test: const chunker = new AstChunker('typescript'); expect(chunker.estimate('function foo() {}')).toBe(1); expect(chunker.estimate('')).toBe(1);

findings.description: maxHeadingDepth test (line 95-106) assertion is weak: expect(chunks.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1) vacuously passes even if H3 is split on. A stronger assertion would count chunks or verify which headings appear as split points.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace with: expect(h3Chunks).toHaveLength(0) — H3 should NOT be a split point when maxHeadingDepth is 2.

backlog_entries: RST heading detection completely broken — multi-line regex can't match line-by-line iteration
Preamble content dropped by both AST and heading chunkers before first declaration/heading
Two test assertions are no-ops (missing .toThrow() matchers)
ChunkerRegistry not sealed despite spec requirement; two competing ChunkerRegistry implementations
Python chunking uses brace-depth tracking incompatible with indentation-based syntax
